title: CSP Input
summary: Reads a Content-Security-Policy the way a browser does, so a policy that looks strict but blocks nothing doesn't ship.
description: Flags 'unsafe-inline' without a nonce, 'unsafe-eval', * / data: / https: in script-src, missing default-src, object-src or base-uri, unquoted keywords, a stray comma that splits the policy, JSONP-hosting allowlisted hosts, typos and report-only traps.
catches: 'unsafe-inline' without a nonce or hash, and 'unsafe-eval'
Wildcards, data: and https: in script-src
Unquoted keywords, missing semicolons and commas that split one header into two policies
Allowlisted hosts known to serve JSONP or AngularJS, and report-only mistakes
limits: Reads the policy text; it does not see your pages or test real script loads
The JSONP/AngularJS host list is a snapshot and may be incomplete
A clean result doesn't mean the site is free of XSS
a11y: Visible <label>; aria-invalid and aria-describedby to an aria-live="polite" status
After a fix, focus moves to the next fix or back to the field
Severity uses icons and text, not colour alone
server: Send the CSP as a response header from your server and monitor violation reports; the policy is enforced by browsers, not by this field.
